title: Radiation does not remove the fitted NCEP ocean heat-gain shift at 60S-60N after 2022
abstract: We tested whether radiation offsets the reduced turbulent ocean heat loss reported after the NCEP sea-temperature input changes. We used all surface heat-flux components in NCEP R1 and R2, one fixed open-ocean mask, and ERSSTv5. A 2000-2025 regression includes regional reference temperature, Nino 3.4, season, trend and two fixed transition levels. The fitted total net downward flux change after February 2023 is +2.93 (+1.06 to +4.81) W/m2 in R1 and +5.17 (+2.54 to +7.80) W/m2 in R2. Intervals are conditional 95 percent HAC intervals. Radiation offsets 54 percent and 25 percent of the turbulent point estimates. Regional net changes have opposite signs, and some earlier matched windows have equally large changes. We test six start-year and trend choices, three regions and matched historical windows. This is a complete surface-energy diagnostic. It extends the earlier turbulent-flux test. There is no independent net-flux reference. Real cloud and circulation changes can contribute to the fitted levels, so the net change is not a measured causal SST-error effect.

display.caption: Surface heat-flux changes on a fixed open-ocean mask. Left: fitted total levels with conditional 95 percent HAC intervals. Right: net-flux seasonal anomalies with a 12-month running mean. Positive flux enters the ocean.
